kak.summary: Review of the Swedish IVA automation committee report, focusing on profitability of automation investment and labour effects: rising share of technical staff, routinised machine-minder work, growing maintenance staff, retraining needs; concludes automation's labour problems concern adjustment more than unemployment. Earliest text in the run with automation as its subject. The quotation reports the reviewed report, not the author's own conclusion.

Short survey (abridged from an HM&V Research Oy report) of expert systems in economic/business applications: rule-based 'fifth-generation' programming for credit decisions, investment advice, sales support and trading; notes US AI companies stumbled by selling Lisp/Prolog and dedicated AI computers, and that expert systems enable 'deeper interaction between human and machine'. Earliest 'tekoäly' in the KAK run (1988).

Review of an ETLA volume on technology diffusion in Finland (NC machine tools, electronics, etc.); summarises Kai Husso's chapter on the diffusion of artificial intelligence into Finland (arrival 1980-84, rapid spread 1985-88; by end-1989 applied by 86 firms, 36 university units and 21 other research units). Second-earliest substantive AI content in KAK after 2/1988.

Stochastic life-cycle model of Finnish social security and taxation solved with reinforcement learning (neural networks), used to estimate employment effects of reforms. AI is the method, not the subject, but the paper discusses the terms 'tekoäly' and 'robotti' and calls RL a candidate for general AI. First KAK title in scope containing 'tekoäly'.
